key_insight: An incremental Deep Energy Method can jointly learn displacement and phase-field evolution for ductile fracture by coupling J2 plasticity with a plasticity-dependent fracture toughness law.
engineering_relevance: This provides a mesh-free, energy-based surrogate for ductile fracture simulation that can reproduce force response, damage growth, and crack paths with accuracy comparable to finite elements.
method: Separate networks: a ReZero residual NN for displacement and localized Gaussian RBFs for the phase field
Minimize the reduced incremental energy alternately over displacement and phase-field variables
Update plastic history locally via radial return and carry constitutive state forward across load steps
evidence_signal: The abstract reports close agreement with finite-element references for force-displacement curves, energy evolution, plastic deformation, and crack propagation.
watch_item: Accuracy becomes more sensitive to the choice of load increments near sudden fracture events, so step-size control is important.
paper_title: A deep energy method formulation for phase-field modelling of ductile fracture
